business_problem: Chatham needed to reduce the routine execution work around capital-markets advisory, trade validation, and internal software delivery while keeping accuracy, auditability, and human judgment central to the workflow.
solution_summary: Chatham uses Codex and GPT-5.6 to turn capital-markets expertise into applications, AI features, and workflow redesign rather than isolated productivity wins. Through its Process Zero consulting model, the firm starts from the desired outcome, defines the minimum inputs and evidence needed, and decides where AI-built tools can take over routine comparison and organization steps while professionals keep judgment-intensive work. One early result is a trade-validation application built with Codex that gathers supporting evidence, compares key transaction terms, flags discrepancies, and is being measured against expert reviewers before wider automation. Chatham also built an internal app platform called Chatham Vibes, while Chatham Onyx uses Codex and multiple GPT-5.6 and GPT-4.1 variants to build, test, and power connected client-facing experiences such as ChatFIN. Together, these systems give advisors faster access to evidence and insight while preserving traceability and oversight.

solution_components.name: Chatham Onyx

data_flow: Trade data, transaction evidence, portfolio information, and internal workflow requirements are fed into Codex-built applications and GPT-powered features. Outputs are compared against expert reviewers or surfaced inside Onyx, where advisors interpret results and approve what reaches clients.
business_outcome: Chatham cut a key validation workflow from 30 minutes to under four, broadened the number of client and employee applications teams can build, and created more capacity for advisors to focus on interpretation and client needs instead of routine assembly work.
